summary: F2: Confirmed session-token replay suspicion—a zero-MFA Turkcell sign-in without a known device occurred while LT-3104 was actively signed in via MEO, indicating possible credential/token misuse and valid-account use. F5: Sign-in volume is dominated by Portugal (10 events), consistent with the user's managed device and VPN egress rather than anomalous geographic spread.

contrastive.explanation: Rejecting F2 would leave no surviving signal and the policy would land on benign — the opposite of the human-review path we chose.

risk.rationale: F2 is CONFIRMED (0.75) suspected session-token replay (T1550.004/T1078.004): a zero-MFA sign-in from Turkcell with no device while the same user is concurrently active on MEO via managed device LT-3104. This is not a weak signal (rules out monitor) and is not fully explained away by the rejected claims (rules out benign): those rejections explain the Turkcell IP/ASN as shared organizational egress/mail relay and the TR event as possible non-interactive mail sync, but they do not resolve the concurrent zero-MFA no-device session alongside an active managed-device VPN session. Evidence is therefore conflicting/insufficient to confirm a complete account takeover chain (rules out contain) and requires human adjudication to distinguish actual session theft/replay from legitimate shared-infrastructure behavior.
escalate_reasons: signals of compromise without a confirmed abuse chain
